title: Pilot Pathfinder — POC Kickoff & Success Criteria
body:
Purpose and context:
This doc is the canonical kickoff note for the Pilot Pathfinder POC with Atlas Retail (hypothetical customer). Goal: validate that Redwood can meet the customer’s inference SLAs, integrate into their uplift pipelines, and achieve an expected unit cost profile for their product recommendation workload. This is a working document — will be iterated after kickoff and the first workshop.

Outcomes we need to prove (explicit success hypotheses):
1) Latency: 95th percentile token latency for the recommended config (seq length 512, batch profile B) <= 180ms at target concurrency (50 concurrent requests) across peak traffic windows.
2) Throughput: Sustained throughput of 800 requests/min with average latency under 120ms during a 30-minute production-like replay.
3) Accuracy/quality: Recommendation hit-rate (business metric supplied by Atlas) does not degrade by >1.5% versus current in-house model on the provided eval set.
4) Cost: Inference unit cost (tokens + infra) is <= 40% of Atlas’s current hosted spend for the same throughput.
5) Integration: End-to-end pipeline can be automated with Atlas CI (sample deploy job) and Redwood’s private control plane in their VPC within the pilot window.
6) Observability: Redwood Console shows token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency traces, and regression alerts configured for the eval set.

Non-goals / out of scope for this POC:
- Full enterprise PA review & legal contract (we will use a pilot agreement).
- Long-term capacity reservation pricing.
- Serving custom model training or model architecture changes; we will serve the customer-provided model artifact(s).

Kickoff agenda (60 minutes):
- 0–5m: Introductions and roles
- 5–15m: Customer goals and business context (customer success lead)
- 15–25m: Proposed test matrix and benchmarks (SE owner)
- 25–40m: Network, security, and infra requirements (engineering/infra)
- 40–50m: Data, eval sets, and acceptance criteria (product/analytics)
- 50–60m: Next steps, owner assignments, and timeline alignment

Key stakeholders and responsibilities:
- Redwood SE Owner: Ava Chen — overall POC owner, coordinates runs, finalizes acceptance checklist.
- Solutions Eng (implementation): Marcus Rivera, Priya Kapoor — infra setup, model onboarding, performance tuning.
- Customer Technical Lead: R. Gupta (Atlas) — provides eval data, approves access, validates biz metrics.
- Customer SRE: M. Hayes — network/VPC peer, load generation coordination.
- Account / CS: Liam O'Neill — program management, commercial checkpoints.

Minimum required access & artifacts from customer (by D+3 after kickoff):
- Example model artifact(s) (weights + config) exported in one of these formats: HF transformers, ONNX, or torchscript.
- A representative eval corpus (CSV or Parquet) with input request, expected outputs, and scoring function specification.
- VPC peering details or temporary test subnet + bastion user for Private pilot, plus KMS scope if using customer keys.
- API key or test credentials and a sandbox account for Redwood Hosted if we use hosted route.

Test matrix (first two weeks):
- Baseline run: run customer-provided model on Redwood default pinned variant at 1x traffic to verify correctness and gather latency numbers.
- Scaling run: increment concurrency to target (50 concurrent) and measure p50/p95/p99 latencies, memory/KV footprint, and tail latencies.
- Replay run: replay 30-minute production-like trace with automated monitoring for errors, token counts, throughput.
- Degradation checks: force fallback scenarios (model variant unavailable, simulated region outage) to verify graceful fallbacks within defined SLOs.
- Cost sensitivity: run synthetic variations of batching, quantization, and KV cache settings to build a cost vs latency curve.

Acceptance criteria (final signoff to be captured in short acceptance note):
- Technical: All success hypotheses (latency, throughput, quality, cost) are met or exceptions documented with remediation plan.
- Operational: Automated deploy job (CI sample) completes end-to-end from commit -> Redwood routing -> successful inference run.
- Security: Customer approves the test network topology, and required logs/keys meet their audit checklist.
- Documentation: Runbook for the pilot handoff (how to rollback, how to scale) delivered and reviewed.

Risks, mitigations, and open questions:
- Risk: Model artifact incompatibility (custom ops) — Mitigation: early artifact smoke test within 48 hours; fallback to containerized HF runtime.
- Risk: Customer cannot share representative eval data due to privacy — Mitigation: allow synthetic but realistic trace; coordinate with CS to anonymize.
- Open question: Which encryption key model will Atlas want to use? (RKMS vs Redwood-managed). Owner: Marcus.
- Open question: Is there an internal cost target per inference or a monthly cap? Owner: Liam to confirm with Sales.

Initial workshop exercises (Day 2, 3-hour working session):
- Exercise A: Fast model smoke — load model, run 100 synthetic requests, validate outputs.
- Exercise B: Latency tuning clinic — try three batching/quantization configs and capture perf metrics.
- Exercise C: Observability walkthrough — set up Redwood Console alerts and run a small replay to validate traces and cost attribution.
- Deliverables at end of workshop: initial perf report, list of tuned configs, and a short decision log.

Measurement & reporting cadence:
- Daily stand-ups (15 minutes) for first week of runs (SE + customer leads).
- Perf report: after each major run (baseline, scale, replay) delivered as a short spreadsheet and one-slide summary.
- Final POC readout: 1-hour presentation including perf results, cost analysis, and recommendation.

Decision log (template entries):
- 2026-01-16: Decided to use Redwood private deployment in Atlas dev VPC for scale runs. Owner: Marcus.
- 2026-01-18: Atlas approved using synthetic anonymized eval set for early tuning. Owner: R. Gupta.

Next steps (first 7 days):
- D+0: Send kickoff notes and owners list (Ava) — DONE.
- D+1: Customer to provide model artifact and one sample eval file (Atlas).
- D+2: Redwood infra team to provision pilot sandbox in customer VPC (Marcus/Priya).
- D+3: Smoke test run and initial perf baseline (SE team).
- D+5: First tuning workshop and perf writeup (all).

Notes to self / reminders for SE team:
- Keep the first two runs lightweight — prioritize getting a clean baseline over perfect tuning.
- Capture exact command lines, container images, and kernel/driver versions — these matter for reproducibility.
- If we see a >10% quality delta, escalate immediately to applied-ml for root-cause.

Appendix: quick checklist
- [ ] Pilot agreement signed (CS)
- [ ] Model artifact received and validated
- [ ] Eval corpus received / anonymization plan in place
- [ ] VPC/subnet and KMS access configured
- [ ] Redwood Console workspace created and linked
- [ ] CI sample job committed to customer repo

Feedback / edits: please add comments inline or ping #se-pilot-pathfinder on Slack.
